name: WifiWatch
description: Watches your Wi-Fi channel, signal and ping and logs every change
readme_summary: Wifi Watch is a Windows 11 tray application written in C# that monitors your Wi-Fi connection's channel, signal strength, and ping latency. It logs network issues, identifies their source (Wi-Fi, home network, provider, or DNS), and notifies users of significant or prolonged problems, including warnings about DFS channel changes due to radar.
key_features: Live status of Wi-Fi, router, and internet
Logs and categorizes network problems (Wi-Fi, home network, provider, DNS)
Intelligent notifications for serious or persistent issues
DFS channel change warnings due to radar
History, speed tests, and provider reports
primary_use_case: To provide users with real-time monitoring and historical logging of their Wi-Fi network performance, identifying and diagnosing connection issues.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant lighthouse keeper on a stormy night, standing in a cozy, modern room with a large window overlooking a turbulent sea. The lighthouse beam, instead of light, is a focused stream of data packets, illuminating different parts of the sea representing Wi-Fi, home network, provider, and DNS. Red warning lights flash on a small, subtle control panel nearby, indicating a problem. The keeper holds a logbook, marking an incident. The repository name 'WifiWatch' is subtly etched on the lighthouse base. The overall mood is one of watchful protection against digital chaos. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a clean, slightly stylized aesthetic, emphasizing clarity and a sense of security.

name: UltraExplorer
description: Native Windows file manager with a zoomable filesystem canvas. C#/.NET, Direct3D 11, colour Tags and split view.
readme_summary: UltraExplorer is a native Windows file manager that visualizes the file system as a zoomable canvas. It allows users to navigate and understand folder hierarchies intuitively by 'flying' into directories while maintaining awareness of the overall structure. The tool integrates familiar file management features with a novel zoomable user interface and quick preview capabilities.
key_features: Zoomable filesystem canvas
Native Windows file manager
Direct3D 11 rendering
Colour Tags for organization
Split view functionality
Quick Look with compact previews (PDF, 3D models, media, text)
Spacebar quick navigation and panning
Familiar Windows Explorer elements (address bar, navigation pane, shell menus)
primary_use_case: To provide an intuitive and visually engaging way to navigate, manage, and understand complex file system hierarchies on Windows.
cover_image_prompt: A cartographer meticulously drawing a vast, intricate map of a sprawling city. Instead of streets, the map depicts interconnected folders and files, with pathways that glow and zoom. The cartographer is shown 'flying' along one of these pathways, entering a specific district (folder) while still seeing the entire city layout around them. Small, glowing icons representing different file types (documents, images, models) are scattered across the map. Subtle UI elements resembling a file explorer's address bar and zoom controls are integrated into the map's border. The overall mood is one of discovery and clarity, with a clean, digital painting style and a vibrant, organized color palette. The repository name 'UltraExplorer' is subtly etched onto the cartographer's tools.

name: inspektor-gadget
description: Inspektor Gadget is a set of tools and framework for data collection and system inspection on Kubernetes clusters and Linux hosts using eBPF
readme_summary: Inspektor Gadget is a framework and toolset for collecting data and inspecting systems on Kubernetes clusters and Linux hosts. It leverages eBPF technology to package, deploy, and run eBPF programs (called Gadgets) encapsulated in OCI images, offering mechanisms for customization and extension.
key_features: Build and package eBPF programs into OCI images (Gadgets)
Targets Kubernetes clusters and Linux hosts
Collect and export data to observability tools
Security mechanisms for Gadget execution control
Automatic enrichment of kernel data to high-level resources
Support for WebAssembly modules for data post-processing and operator customization
Multiple operation modes: CLI, client-server, API, embeddable Golang library
primary_use_case: System inspection and data collection on Kubernetes and Linux hosts using eBPF.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant digital detective, wearing a futuristic headset, stands at a bustling crossroads representing a Kubernetes cluster. They are holding a magnifying glass that reveals glowing, intricate data streams flowing from various containers and nodes. The magnifying glass highlights specific events, like a file being opened or a network connection being made, represented by small, clear icons. Subtle eBPF-like energy tendrils connect the detective to the data streams. The background shows abstract representations of Linux hosts and cloud infrastructure. The overall mood is one of insightful observation and control, with a clean, modern aesthetic and a color palette of blues, greens, and purples. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear, defined elements.

name: ubuntu-cleaner
description: Ubuntu Cleaner is a tool that makes it easy to clean your ubuntu system.
readme_summary: Ubuntu Cleaner is a Python-based tool designed to free up disk space and remove private information on Ubuntu systems. It offers a user-friendly way to clear various caches, uninstall unneeded packages, and remove old system components.
key_features: Clear browser cache
Clear APT cache
Clear thumbnail cache
Remove unneeded packages
Remove old kernels
Remove old installers
primary_use_case: System cleaning and disk space optimization for Ubuntu operating systems.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly robot gardener meticulously pruning a digital tree representing an Ubuntu system. The robot is carefully removing dead branches (old kernels, unneeded packages) and clearing away digital dust bunnies (caches) from the tree's leaves. Small, glowing icons representing browsers and installers float nearby, being tidied up. The background is a clean, organized digital landscape with subtle lines of code and data streams flowing neatly. The overall mood is one of efficiency and tidiness, with a bright, clean color palette. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear, friendly character design and subtle technological accents.

name: straps
readme_summary: Straps is a comprehensive Bash testing harness that provides over 80 utility functions designed to streamline testing for cloud-native development, Docker containers, Kubernetes, system administration, and DevOps automation. It integrates seamlessly with the Bats testing framework, offering robust validation for data types, network operations, file systems, and cloud infrastructure components.
key_features: Data Type Validation (integers, floats, strings, unsigned integers)
String Operations (starts with, ends with, contains)
Network Testing (TCP/UDP connectivity, DNS resolution)
File System Operations (existence, permissions)
Docker & Container Testing (status, images, ports, volumes, networks)
Kubernetes Resource Validation (naming, labels, annotations, namespaces)
Service Discovery & Health Checks
Security Features (SSL/TLS certificates, SSH keys, SELinux)
Cross-Platform Compatibility
Seamless BATS Integration
primary_use_case: Automating and simplifying the testing of cloud-native applications, Docker containers, Kubernetes deployments, and general system administration tasks using Bash scripts and the Bats testing framework.
cover_image_prompt: A master craftsman, a seasoned DevOps engineer, meticulously assembling a complex, glowing network of interconnected pipes and gears representing cloud infrastructure. They are using a specialized set of digital blueprints and tools to validate each connection and component. Small, stylized icons representing Docker containers and Kubernetes pods are being tested and validated as they are integrated into the larger system. The scene is set in a clean, modern workshop with subtle code snippets and data streams flowing in the background, emphasizing precision and automation. The overall style should be a vibrant 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear visual metaphors for testing and validation.
